XXVII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|367}}</noinclude>litle thou persuadest me to become a {{sc|C h r i s t i a n}}. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=29}}† And Paul said, I vvish of God, both in litle, and in much, not only thee, but also al that heare this day, to become such as I am also, except these bandes. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=30}}† And the king rose vp, and the President, and Bernice, and they that sate by them.

{{verse|chapter=26|verse=31}}† And going a side, they spake among them selues, saying, That this man hath done nothing vvorthie of death or bandes. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=32}}† And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might be released, if he had not appealed to Caesar.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXVII.}}}}}}

{{c|''What a dangerous nauigation he had tovvards Rome: and that by his prediction and counsel the ship might haue been saued. And for his sake (as God also reuealed to him before) al the companie vvas preserued, being 276 persons.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=27|verse=1}}}}ND after it vvas decreed that he should saile into Italie, and that Paul vvith other prisoners should be deliuered to a Centurion named Iulius, of the band Augusta, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=2}}† vve going vp into a ship of Adrumétum, beginning to saile about the places of Asia, loosed from the land, Aristarchus the Macedonian of Thessalonica continuing vvith vs. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=3}}† And the day folovving vve came to Sidon. And Iulius intreating Paul courteously, permitted him to goe to his frendes, and to take care of him self. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=4}}† And vvhen vve had loosed thence, vve sailed vnder Cypres: because the vvindes vvere contrarie. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=5}}† And sailing the sea of Cilicia and Pamphilia, vve came to {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`Myra''}}`Lystra', vvhich is in Lycia: {{verse|chapter=27|verse=6}}† and there the Centurion finding a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italie, remoued vs into it. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=7}}† And vvhereas many daies vve sailed slovvly, & vvere scarse come ouer against Gnidus, the vvinde hindering vs, vve sailed neere Crete by Salmóne: {{verse|chapter=27|verse=8}}† and vvith much a doe sailing by it, vve came into a certaine place that is called Good-hauens, nigh to the vvhich vvas a citie Thalassa.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=9}}† And vvhen much time vvas spent, and vvhereas novv it vvas not safe sailing, because the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ It may signifie the Iewes fast of the seuenth moneth September, after vvhich the nauigation vvas perilous, vvinter approching.}}∷ fast novv vvas past, Paul comforted them, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=10}}† saying to them, Ye men, I see that the sailing beginneth to be vvith hurt and much damage not only of the lading and the ship, but also of our liues. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=11}}† But the<noinclude>{{rh|||Centurion}}</noinclude>
